sum: GFT Technologies reported stronger growth and profitability for the first nine months of 2026 on Thursday, November 12. In its financial release, the company said revenue rose 7 percent to EUR 700.9 million from January through September.

Adjusted EBIT increased 16 percent to EUR 52.9 million, lifting the adjusted EBIT margin by 0.6 percentage points to 7.6 percent. Earnings before taxes rose 24 percent to EUR 40.0 million, while net income advanced 27 percent to EUR 28.5 million.

GFT said the Americas and APAC segment grew revenue 15 percent to EUR 371.5 million, supported by Brazil and Colombia. The European business gained momentum in the third quarter, when revenue increased 5 percent.

The Wynxx Agentic AI Platform generated influenced revenue of EUR 38.1 million in Software Engineering during the period. The Wynxx Business Process Suite contributed EUR 24.3 million. GFT also highlighted a Deutsche Bank core banking modernization mandate and an Itaú Unibanco deployment that reduced migration time by up to 70 percent, according to the company.

GFT raised its 2026 outlook to revenue of EUR 945 million and adjusted EBIT of EUR 72 million. The company expects an adjusted EBIT margin of 7.6 percent and EBT of EUR 56 million. The order backlog stood 22 percent above the prior-year level at September 30.

Itaú Unibanco Shares Fall 22.13 Percent Amid Brazil Election Fallout
sum: Shares of Itaú Unibanco Holding S.A. (ITUB) opened down 22.13 percent on October 26, as Brazil's presidential election outcome unsettled financial markets and weakened investor confidence in the country's fiscal outlook. According to TradingKey, the sell-off reflected political uncertainty, currency depreciation, and capital outflows from emerging markets rather than a deterioration in the bank's core operations.

Investors had previously pushed Brazilian banking stocks higher on expectations of a more market-friendly fiscal direction. Following the election results, markets reversed those positions as concerns mounted over future government spending, potential tax policy changes, and delays to structural reforms, TradingKey reported.

The political shift also affected expectations for domestic economic growth and monetary policy. Investors reassessed Brazil's fiscal trajectory, while the Brazilian real weakened against the U.S. dollar, reducing dollar-denominated returns for foreign shareholders.

TradingKey reported that Brazilian equity benchmarks and regional exchange-traded funds experienced institutional capital outflows as global investors reduced their exposure to emerging markets. Itaú Unibanco, Latin America's largest private financial institution by assets, was particularly exposed to changes in international investment flows because of its position in the Brazilian financial market.

Separately, Itaú Unibanco announced an agreement to acquire full ownership of generative artificial intelligence company NeoSpace AI. The transaction is intended to strengthen the bank's proprietary technology infrastructure and improve its digital services for customers.

According to details cited by TradingKey, the acquisition is valued at BRL 2.925 billion, approximately $580 million, and involves an all-cash payment structure. The transaction also includes deferred payment obligations over five years and remains subject to regulatory approvals from Brazil's Administrative Council for Economic Defense (CADE) and the Central Bank of Brazil.
Despite the sharp share-price decline, TradingKey described the bank's underlying financial position as solid, citing healthy profit margins, stable asset quality, and high return on equity.

sum: Brazil Stock Market Today: Brazilian stocks and currency faced selling pressure on Monday, October 26 following the win of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the re-election. He beat right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff. Major Brazilian companies like Petrobras, Itaú Unibanco and Banco Bradesco saw declines in US premarket trading as investors reconsidered the country’s economic future.

The Superior Electoral Court said that Lula received 51.79% of votes while Flávio Bolsonaro got 48.21%. This outcome surprised market predictions of a change in government and a move toward stricter fiscal policies.

Early trading reports showed that US-listed Petrobras shares dropped 22%. Itaú Unibanco and Banco Bradesco were among the banking stocks that fell between 23% and 29%. These numbers are movements and should not be seen as the final closing losses for these companies on Brazil’s B3 exchange.
Reuters also said that November futures, for the real dropped 10% during Asian trading. The Tokyo-listed Nomura NF Ibovespa Link exchange-traded fund, which follows equities fell 15%.
Brazil Election Result 2026: Why Markets Reacted To Lula’s Victory; Ibovespa Falls

Investors had been preparing for a win by Flávio Bolsonaro, who came first in the opening round. Brazilian assets had jumped before the round because people thought a new government might tighten spending.

Before the result Brazilian stocks had finished almost 7 percent higher than they were before the first round. The real had risen 5 percent against the US dollar. Interest‑rate futures also showed that people expected tighter fiscal rules to lower borrowing costs eventually.

items.t: Stock Market Today, Oct. 7: Itaú Unibanco Falls on Profit-Taking After Brazil Election Rally
sum: Itaú Unibanco Holding (ITUB -1.67%), a Brazil-focused universal bank, closed at $9.74, down 4.04%. Investors appeared to take profits after a Brazil-election-themed note and a multi-year high stock price. Investors will be closely watching the Brazilian runoff election round next.
Trading volume reached 40.0 million shares, coming in about 64% above its three-month average of 24.3 million shares. Itaú Unibanco Holding IPO'd in 2002 and has grown 825% since going public.

The S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.36%) closed at 7,801, down 0.23%, and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +0.83%) closed at 27,539, down 0.22%. Among Brazilian diversified banking and financial services peers, Nu Holdings (NU -0.09%) closed at $15.58, down 0.51%, while Banco Santander (SAN -1.05%) closed at $13.66, down 2.50%, showing softer sentiment across the group.

Yesterday, Itaú stock soared to its highest level seen in more than five years. Today's drop implies profit-taking, especially with the final results from the Brazilian presidential election still to be determined.

A runoff election will be held after no candidate won the necessary 50% majority in the first round of voting on Oct. 4. But conservative candidate Flávio Bolsonaro surprised pollsters by receiving more votes than incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

That was the catalyst for a rally in Brazilian stocks, including bank names. Analysts responded with predictions that recurring net income will jump, and Itaú shares spiked to over $10 per share for the first time in more than five years.

Fiscal impulse remains smaller but positive in 2027, Itaú says
sum: Income transfers to households are expected to be main factor providing additional support to economic activity, bank says in a study

The contribution of Brazil’s fiscal and quasi-fiscal policies to GDP growth is expected to slow but remain positive in 2027, mainly because income transfers to households, which have a greater impact on economic activity, are likely to expand at a pace similar to that of 2026. That is the conclusion of a report by Itaú Unibanco economists Marina Garrido, Natalia Cotarelli, Pedro Schneider, and Thales Guimarães.

The analysis comes as economists intensify their debate over the possibility of a sharper slowdown in Brazil’s economy in 2027, depending on fiscal and credit policies. At the same time, analysts acknowledge that fiscal and quasi-fiscal stimulus during an election period would further undermine Brazil’s already fragile fiscal position.

At the beginning of the year, the market median forecast for Brazil’s GDP growth in 2027 stood at 1.8%, according to the Central Bank’s Focus survey. It has now been revised down to 1.57%. Some economists expect even weaker growth.

At the XP Expert event in July, portfolio manager Bruno Serra of Itaú Asset Management said he was working with GDP growth below 1% in 2027 and that the risk of a recession next year could not be ruled out, according to Valor’s Intraday blog.

XP projects 1% growth, citing “the end of the effects of short-term stimulus and the likely cyclical pullback in credit,” according to a report. BTG Pactual forecasts 1.1%, while warning that growth could come in even lower, according to a report by the team led by chief economist Mansueto Almeida and head of macro research Tiago Berriel. “The outlook for next year is more challenging, with interest rates remaining at an even more contractionary level and fiscal stimulus close to neutral,” they wrote.

More recently, ASA lowered its 2027 GDP growth forecast to 1.5% from 2%, citing expectations of a “hangover” from the fiscal and quasi-fiscal stimulus seen in 2026, which should reduce support for demand in an environment that will still feature high interest rates.

Swift Goes Live with New Blockchain-Based Ledger
sum: - Swift launched a blockchain-based ledger that lets banks move tokenized deposits across borders 24/7 before completing final settlement through existing banking systems.

- The ledger is designed to make blockchain interoperable with bank infrastructure, giving financial institutions a shared layer for digital money without requiring them to abandon current rails or compliance processes.
- Seventeen global banks will participate in the initial pilot, moving Swift’s blockchain work from prototype to live testing with major transaction banks across six continents.

Swift has officially launched its new blockchain-based ledger that will support 24/7 cross-border payments with tokenized deposits, enabling funds to move in any regulated form, anywhere, with a high level of security.

The shared, blockchain-based ledger offers banks an orchestration layer for bank-issued tokenized deposits on their own ledgers. The blockchain ledger enables banks to move funds for customers 24 hours a day, seven days a week, before completing final settlement through the banks’ existing systems. In addition to always-on settlement, banks can offer clients global liquidity while maintaining compliance, credit, risk, and control standards.

“With our new ledger capability, we’re extending the trust and stability of established finance into the frontiers of digital money,” said Swift Chief Business Officer Thierry Chilosi. “It allows tokenized value to move across borders with the velocity and flexibility modern commerce expects, while maintaining the same high levels of resiliency, security, and compliance global finance requires. The strong support from banks shows the practical value of this approach—one that will help scale benefits globally while creating a foundation for future innovation in areas like programmable money and agentic commerce.”

Unlike other new payments technology, Swift’s ledger brings blockchain-based payments into the infrastructure banks already use. While previous digital money efforts were fragmented across pilots, private networks, and bank-specific systems, Swift’s approach gives banks a shared layer for moving tokenized value across borders while preserving the compliance, resiliency, and settlement processes that each region requires.

items.t: Petrobras and Vale Fuel EWZ’s Huge Payouts, But You Shouldn’t Expect Consistency
sum: The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (NYSEARCA:EWZ) has rallied alongside Brazilian equities, lifting shares roughly 48% over the past year. EWZ pays a variable semi-annual distribution funded by dividends from the largest Brazilian companies. After a powerful 2024 through 2025 commodity…

EWZ tracks the MSCI Brazil 25/50 Index and holds roughly 50 large- and mid-cap Brazilian stocks, with iron-ore miner Vale, state oil company Petrobras, and the country’s big banks (Itaú Unibanco, Banco Bradesco, Banco do Brasil) typically commanding the largest weights. The fund collects whatever those companies pay in Brazilian reais, converts proceeds to dollars, deducts the 0.59% expense ratio, and passes the rest along twice a year. The distribution is whatever Brazilian corporate boards decide to send out, translated through the BRL/USD rate.

That mechanic explains the recent swings. The June 2025 distribution came in at $0.52, the December 2025 payment at $1.03, plus a January 2026 reconciliation of $0.11. What matters is whether the underlying companies still have the cash to pay.

Petrobras and Vale dominate distribution capacity. WTI crude sits at almost $110 a barrel, in the 98th percentile of its 12-month range against a one-year average of $69. Petrobras is a dividend machine when oil holds above $80 and a dividend cutter when it sinks below $60, so current levels point to elevated payouts ahead. Iron ore has stayed firm enough to keep Vale’s variable dividend policy active.

The risk is exactly that dependency. Brazilian commodity producers do not smooth payouts the way US dividend aristocrats do. Petrobras moved to a free-cash-flow-linked formula in 2023, and Vale already pays based on a percentage of operating cash flow. When commodities turn, the dividend turns with them, often within one or two quarters.

The Financials sleeve, the index’s largest, has been the steadier income contributor. Itaú and Banco do Brasil run healthy capital ratios and high-teens returns on equity, with interim dividend and interest-on-capital payments more predictable than commodity payouts.
Currency does the rest of the work. The real currently fetches roughly $0.20, well off its 2020 through 2021 lows. A weaker real shrinks every dollar distribution even when reais payouts grow.

2026 Stock Market Winners: 3 Breakout Picks With Big Upside
sum: Investors can improve results by taking a more active approach to stock selection by focusing on potential breakout opportunities within clearly defined price ranges. Under this strategy, a stock is sold if it falls below the lower boundary, while a move above the upper boundary signals strength and an opportunity to stay invested and ride further upside momentum.
Using this framework, Seanergy Maritime Holdings Corp SHIP, Itaú Unibanco Holding S.A. ITUB and Chatham Lodging Trust CLDT stand out as potential stocks on the verge of a massive breakout in 2026.

To pick a breakout stock, calculate support and resistance levels. A support level is the lower bound for stock price movements, while a resistance level is the maximum price the stock trades at over a considerable period.

In other words, demand for a stock is at its lowest at its support level, which means most traders are willing to sell it. At the resistance level, most traders are willing to go long on the stock, meaning they would like to add it to their portfolio. The key to identifying breakout stocks is to zero in on those on the verge of a breakout or those that have just broken above the resistance level.

The primary risk associated with such a strategy is that the decision to buy an apparent breakout candidate has been incorrectly timed. When a stock moves above the resistance level, it should be a highly prized commodity for traders. However, whether such a breakout is genuine is another matter altogether.

For a bona fide breakout, the stock's earlier resistance barrier should become its new support level. This only happens if the established trading channel is tested by observing long-term price trends. The strength of the support and resistance levels can be ascertained only through such a study. Despite the risk of misidentification, correctly identifying such stocks can yield considerable returns, even at a price that may not seem attractive at first glance.

items.t: 3 Foreign Bank Stocks to Invest in From the Booming Industry
sum: Global lenders have been streamlining operations, which has improved revenue quality and cost efficiency. Though these restructuring efforts may raise near-term expenses, they are expected to drive sustainable growth. Meanwhile, lower interest rates (as most central banks ease monetary policy) are likely to spur borrowing and reduce funding costs, supporting banks' top line.

Although uneven economic recovery across developed and emerging markets has weighed on revenue expansion for players in the Zacks Foreign Banks Industry, firms like HSBC Holdings HSBC, Itau Unibanco Holding ITUB and Barclays PLC BCS will gain from the business restructuring efforts and gradually declining rates.

The Zacks Foreign Banks Industry consists of overseas banks with operations in the United States. Since a foreign banking organization may have federal and state-chartered offices in the country, the Federal Reserve plays a major role in supervising its U.S. operations. In addition to providing a broad range of products and services to customers in the United States, banks offer financial services to corporate clients having businesses in the country. Financial firms establish relations with U.S. corporations operating in their home countries. Some units of foreign banks offer a broad range of wholesale and retail services and conduct money-market transactions for their parent organizations. Some industry players are involved in developing only specialized services like wealth/asset management and investment banking.

Continued Restructuring Efforts to Support Growth: Many global lenders have been undertaking business-restructuring initiatives to improve efficiency. Banks have exited non-core geographies, scaled back low-return business lines and redeployed capital toward higher-growth segments, such as wealth management, transaction banking and digital platforms. By reallocating capital to stronger franchises and deepening client relationships, these banks are enhancing revenue quality, improving net interest margins and generating more stable fee-based income streams.
Also, restructuring has translated into leaner operating models and better cost discipline.

sum: Nu Holdings Ltd. (NYSE:NU) is among the 12 Best Digital Currency and Payments Stocks to Buy Right Now.

Bloomberg reported on February 5, 2026, that David Velez, CEO of Nu Holdings Ltd. (NYSE:NU), is working to expand Nubank, one of the most valuable financial firms in Latin America, to a global clientele of over 127 million. It includes almost 60% of Brazil's adult population. The company's shares are valued higher than those of traditional banks, and in the third quarter, their return on equity was 31%, compared to Itau Unibanco's 23.3%. Velez's super-voting shares give it control over about 75% of the voting power. Velez noted that while Nubank is still focused on Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, the recent conditional acceptance for a US national bank license is a long-term potential rather than a short-term goal.

The US expansion, referred to as "Act Three," aims to get a complete banking license before expanding services. Although analysts acknowledge Nubank's advantages in technology, low operating costs, and user experience, they caution that profits could be lower in the fiercely competitive US market. items.t: Federal court backs Itaú Unibanco in R$36bn tax dispute
sum: TRF-1 ruling blocks appeal in Brazil’s largest case before tax board Carf

Itaú Unibanco is closer to overturning a R$36.5 billion tax assessment. In a 3–2 ruling, judges at Brazil’s Federal Regional Court for the 1st Region (TRF-1) decided that the Superior Chamber of the Administrative Council of Tax Appeals (Carf) should not hear the Treasury’s appeal of a previous decision favoring the bank. The Office of the Attorney General of the National Treasury (PGFN) intends to challenge the ruling.

After the vote, PGFN head, Anelize Lenzi, said the office will consider whether to file a motion for clarification with TRF-1 or take the case to the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) or even the Supreme Federal Court (STF) on constitutional grounds.
This is the largest case ever heard at Carf. If the TRF-1 decision stands, it would seal the bank’s victory.

The bank initially prevailed in 2017, when the 1st Panel of Carf’s 2nd Chamber in the 1st Section ruled 5–3 to strike down the charge. The Treasury appealed and awaited a review by Carf’s Superior Chamber.

To move forward, Carf appeals must cite a “paradigm”—a similar case previously decided differently. The then-president of Carf’s 1st Section rejected the Treasury’s proposed paradigm, prompting PGFN to appeal and Itaú to seek a court order to block the appeal.
As a result, the legal question that had stalled Carf’s ruling may now make the 2017 decision final.

IG4 takes over bank debt at Braskem as Novonor loses control
sum: Asset manager IG4, led by Paulo Mattos, announced on Monday (15) that it has acquired about R$20 billion in Braskem-related bank claims through a direct lending fund (FIDC).

The claims were previously held by Itaú Unibanco, Santander, Bradesco, Banco do Brasil, and the Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES), and had been pledged as collateral by Novonor (formerly Odebrecht) to the lenders.

Under the agreement between IG4 and Novonor—currently the controlling shareholder of one of the world’s largest petrochemical companies—the Bahia-based group committed to transfer all of its controlling common shares in Braskem to a private equity fund (FIP), in exchange for a partial settlement of the claims held by the FIDC.

As a result, Novonor will retain only a 4% stake in Braskem, represented by preferred shares, with no governance rights or additional prerogatives beyond those provided under Brazil’s Corporations Law.

According to a securities filing, the transaction structure was made possible by the consensual release of fiduciary alienations on the shares and includes a 60-day exclusivity period to execute the definitive documentation.

The deal is subject to approval by Brazil’s antitrust authority, the Administrative Council for Economic Defense (CADE). Once cleared, a new shareholders’ agreement will be signed between the FIP and Petrobras, establishing joint control of Braskem. Novonor will not be part of the new arrangement.
The filing also said Braskem’s current management team and advisors will remain unchanged, ensuring full operational continuity.

items.t: Itaú Private hits R$1tn in AUM with global strategy shift
sum: Private banking arm expands client base, embraces tech, and grows international share amid Brazil’s changing wealth landscape

Itaú Private surpassed R$1 trillion in assets under management and administration two years ahead of schedule, with 70% allocated in the domestic market and 30% abroad. The achievement follows a broad strategic overhaul, said global head Fernando Beyruti, and reflects a response to changes in global wealth management.
“We hit pause in the second half of last year and, with the help of a consulting firm, reassessed how the wealth management industry was evolving,” Beyruti told Valor.

The milestone, reached in November, gives Itaú Private a 30.8% share of Brazil’s private banking market, up from 28% in 2022. By the end of 2025, the firm expects to attract another R$50 billion in new assets, its largest ever annual net inflow.

Key changes included lowering the minimum investable assets required to join, adopting a global investment approach, “onshore and offshore, without conflict,” said Beyruti, and making significant investments in technology.

The Brazilian wealth management market has seen intense activity. BTG Pactual, for example, acquired Julius Baer’s local business for R$615 million this year and took over JGP’s wealth unit in April. Together, BTG’s personal banking and private divisions now manage R$1.1 trillion, although BTG does not break out the data as Itaú does.
The start of taxation on closed-end exclusive funds in 2024 also triggered a shift in behavior. While these structures haven’t been abandoned by ultra-wealthy clients, their relevance has diminished.
